title: Godot compute shader pragma breaks external editors
body:
### Tested versions

Encountered in v4.3.stable.mono.official [77dcf97d8]

I don't believe this is version specific, rather a design issue of compute shader support.

### System information

Godot v4.3.stable.mono - Freedesktop SDK 24.08 (Flatpak runtime) - Wayland - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 7700S (RADV NAVI33) - AMD Ryzen 7 7840HS w/ Radeon 780M Graphics (16 Threads)

### Issue description

Godot compute shaders require the Godot-specific `#[compute]` pragma at the top of GLSL files for the editor to import them.

This requirement conflicts with the GLSL specification: https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/GLSLangSpec.4.60.pdf page 16 states:

> The #version directive must occur in a shader before anything else, except for comments and whitespace.

This means that Godot compute shaders, despite being written in GLSL, are not valid GLSL according to the spec. As a result, every editor I've tried with GLSL support fails to parse Godot compute shaders correctly: they report an error on `#[compute]` because the first statement must be `#version`, and then turn off most IDE support because they don't know what version of GLSL to use.

Given that Godot doesn't have a builtin GLSL editor, this seems like a major usability issue for Godot compute shaders.

To be compatible with the GLSL spec, I suggest also supporting a comment-form of the Godot pragma, e.g. `//[compute]`. This would be compatible with standard GLSL, and still allow Godot to identify compute shaders easily.

### Steps to reproduce

Follow the compute shader tutorial in the manual. As instructed in the tutorial, open an external editor (I tried VScode with every GLSL extension I could find, and Emacs with glsl-mode) to write the compute shader. Observe that linting and editor support degrades as soon as you add `#[compute]` to the file, because the file is no longer valid GLSL.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A, this is not a project-specific issue, it's a design issue with Godot compute shader processing.
